nodes.body: This only checks the destination surface. If `foreground` has already been disposed, the size checks still succeed and the loop then calls the private `foreground.GetPaddedRowSpanBytes`, which bypasses the disposal guard and reads the disposed buffer. That violates the new lifetime contract and would become a use-after-return once the buffer is pooled; check the foreground's disposed state after the null check (and add a regression test).

This parent requirement also promises that disposal releases the pixel buffer, while the implementation deliberately only marks the plain managed buffer as disposed. Leaving the parent wording unchanged preserves the same traceability discrepancy even if the child requirement is corrected; align it with the current logical-unavailability contract or defer resource release to the pooling follow-up.

The PR description and `Surface` documentation explicitly state that this release does not release anything from `Dispose()` because the buffer is still a plain managed array, but this requirement says disposal shall release pixel-buffer resources. The linked tests only verify idempotency and guards, so this wording makes ReqStream claim behavior that the implementation intentionally does not provide; describe making the buffer unavailable instead, or defer the release requirement to the pooling change.

`Clear` is a public buffer-mutating member and receives a disposal guard here, but the new disposal test matrix and traceability lists omit a `Clear`-after-dispose case. Add `Surface_Clear_AfterDispose_ThrowsObjectDisposedException` and include it in the corresponding verification/requirement test lists so the documented “every” guarantee covers this member too.

This issue also appears on line 732 of the same file.

`Crop` returns another owning `Surface`, so this sample still leaves that new surface undisposed even though the PR updates the examples to teach disposal. Bind the crop result with `using var` as well; otherwise the sample does not model the lifetime contract for derived surfaces.

This design contract enumerates the public buffer-touching members that throw after disposal but omits `Clear`, which is now guarded at `Surface.cs:672`. Include `Clear` here so the design documentation agrees with the implementation and verification requirements.

The disposal documentation omits `Clear`, even though it is a public buffer-touching member and is guarded by the new contract. As written, this user-facing list is incomplete and conflicts with the following “any other public buffer-touching member” exception statement; include `Clear` in the list.

`Crop` returns another owning `Surface`, so this updated example still leaves the cropped surface undisposed. Since this section now teaches `using var` for `Surface` lifetimes, bind the crop result with `using var` too.

This lambda is passed to xUnit's `Record.Exception(Action)`, but a bare property access is not a valid statement expression for an `Action` lambda, so the test will not compile. Assign the value (for example, `() => _ = canvas.Surface`) or rely on the following `Assert.Same` access to verify that no exception is thrown.
